speaker: narrator
text: Act III: Trials and Revelations

speaker: narrator
text: You said it aloud in the castle courtyard, with the vision still fading: “He took them. That is why they vanished, and that is why he wants me.” Sir Cedric did not correct you. Nobody has, and so it has become what you believe: Malakar took your parents, and now he is coming for you.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira came to Greendale the night of the vision. She had felt the amulet open to the forest, she said, and knew. In the castle courtyard she drew a circle in chalk, and the three of you stepped out of it into her hut in Willowbrook, the herbs still swinging from the beam. She has not yet said how a village healer learned to do that.

speaker: narrator
text: Now she is the only one who can say what must be done next, and where the road to Malakar begins.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira's Hut

speaker: narrator
text: A fragrant hut filled with drying herbs and mysterious potions. Shelves overflow with bottles, roots, and colorful flowers. The air is thick with the scent of lavender and sage. Sunlight streams through stained glass, painting the walls in shifting hues. Mira herself moves gracefully among her concoctions, her eyes bright with knowledge and kindness.

speaker: mira
text: Elior. Malakar is draining King Alden's life to break Eldoria's wards, and the king grows weaker every day.

speaker: mira
text: Three relics can stand against him: the Crystal of Light, the Phoenix Feather and the Dragon's Scale. We will fetch them one at a time.

speaker: mira
text: Before we go, take this, and read it. Then we can leave.

speaker: mira
text: Say the word, and I will draw the first circle.

speaker: mira
text: On the road, ask me what you need to. I may not be able to answer all of it yet.

speaker: narrator
text: (Ask her with: say parents, say malakar, say amulet or say grandmother to Mira.)

speaker: narrator
text: New main quest

speaker: narrator
text: The Three Virtues

speaker: narrator
text: Prove Courage, Wisdom, and Selflessness by recovering the three relics: the Crystal of Light, the Phoenix Feather, and the Dragon's Scale.

speaker: mira
text: Elior, as you journey to the relic sites, keep your eyes open for traces of the past. Your parents left marks upon this world—fragments of their story that Malakar could not erase. In the depths where courage is tested, on the heights where wisdom burns, and in the shadows where sacrifice echoes, you may find the truth of how they hid you from his sight. The three testimonies will reveal what love can accomplish against the darkest power.

speaker: mira
text: Before we proceed, Elior, you should read the note I gave you. It contains important guidance about your journey that you may find... enlightening.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Mira knows the way. I know how to stand in front of you. Between us, that will have to do.

speaker: narrator
text: New side quest

speaker: narrator
text: Echoes of the Hidden Bond

speaker: narrator
text: Your parents once walked these same paths in their own desperate search for the three relics. As you face the trials they faced, you may discover traces of their passage.

speaker: narrator
text: ○ In the depths where courage is tested, echoes of the past linger.

speaker: narrator
text: ○ On the heights where wisdom burns, their words may still echo.

speaker: narrator
text: ○ In the shadows where sacrifice dwells, ancient memories await.

speaker: mira
text: The hour is upon us, Elior. We will draw the first circle at the Tidal Causeway, where moonlight marries the sea.

speaker: mira
text: When the air folds and the mist closes, breathe. It will pass in a heartbeat.

speaker: narrator
text: Tidal Causeway

speaker: narrator
text: Thin causeways of old stone lift from the black water like ribs. Moonlight skims the wet stones; salt and wind carry half‑heard songs. Broken arches stand like quiet mouths, guarding what the sea keeps.

speaker: mira
text: This place keeps its secrets in salt and song. Within the Sunken Ruins lies the Crystal of Light—an old relic that answers to courage. It parts veils and steadies the spirit. When you stand before the tide-born guardian, speak your vow and let it steady you.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Salt and old stone. Give me a wall to hold and I would know what to do. Here I just follow you.

speaker: mother
text: Malakar, our friend —

speaker: mother
text: We made the relics together, the three of us, and swore they would only ever guard, never take. Now you speak of time as if it were a door you could open and close again. It is not a door. It is a wound, and what comes through it will not stop at saving us.

speaker: mother
text: We are not afraid of what is coming. We are afraid of what you will become to stop it. Wait with us. Be patient, for once. If you will not, we will stand against you, not as your enemies but as your friends, and as Wardens of the Dawn.

speaker: mother
text: — Aren and Lysa

speaker: malakar
text: You would have me wait while you die. — M.

speaker: mira
text: Lysa's hand. She always crossed her sevens.

speaker: narrator
text: You take the Sea-Sealed Letter. You carefully fold the letter — a plea to a friend, kept by the sea.

speaker: narrator
text: ✓ Depths of the Sunken Ruins: You found traces of your parents' first passage, revealing their past as Malakar's apprentices and the moment they chose to defy him.

speaker: narrator
text: You take the Rusted Locker Key. Its teeth are ragged with corrosion; it might fit, but the lock has long since fused.

speaker: narrator
text: Shoreline Markers

speaker: narrator
text: The shore here is quiet and cold. Weathered steles rise from the sand, their worn faces full of shallow marks. Salt and time have smudged many lines, but faint moon sigils still show when the tide drops. Loose pale flakes sit in the grooves; they shimmer like old stars. When the moon is high, the stones seem to hum with a slow, patient voice—an old magic tied to the sea.

speaker: narrator
text: Tideward Sigils

speaker: narrator
text: Ancient warding pillars stand along the drowned causeway — relics of coastal rites that once bent the tides to human will. You must cleanse and activate them by engraving a full Moon Sigil to steady the flood wards and gain safe passage to the sanctum.

speaker: narrator
text: You take the Moon Rune Shards. The shards whisper with tide-salt; they leave a faint dust on your fingers.

speaker: narrator
text: Outer Wards

speaker: narrator
text: The courtyard lies half-swallowed by the sea. Three ancient pillars rise from the black water, their faces scored with shallow marks. Brine beads along the carved lines and they catch the moon in small rings of light. The air here tastes of old promises and slow tides.

speaker: narrator
text: Side quest complete

speaker: narrator
text: You cleansed the pillars and set the Moon Rune shards—the Moon Sigil resonates and the flood wards steady, granting safe passage toward the sanctum.

speaker: narrator
text: Collapsed Pier

speaker: narrator
text: The pier surrenders to the tide. Warped planks gape and blackened vaults yawn where light forgets to go. Barnacled timbers rise like buried ribs, and the water sings a low, patient counting of losses.

speaker: narrator
text: Barnacles crust the seam; the fused lock will not yield to a mundane key.

speaker: narrator
text: The Pier Warden nods slowly.

speaker: pier warden
text: You've done right by the pillars. There's a fused locker down in the vaults; I tried a key once but it stuck. Key's no good alone, and magic's no good alone. It wants both.

speaker: pier warden
text: You'll have seen the causeway. Birds by the hundred, and the surf gone grey. I've known bad seasons on this coast, forty years of them. It's only a bad season, isn't it? Tell me the sea will mend on its own.

speaker: narrator
text: The mechanism is freed; the door can be opened.

speaker: narrator
text: With a brittle crack the door gives, revealing three prism lanterns gleaming behind veils of silt.

speaker: narrator
text: The door hangs open and the interior is still and cold, silt motes drifting inside.

speaker: narrator
text: Submerged Antechamber

speaker: narrator
text: The hall lies half-swallowed by tide and time. Salt-smoothed stone arches bear weathered carvings that pulse with a cold, inner glow. A hush hangs in the air as if the sea itself listens; faint, distant echoes suggest something patient and watchful beyond the veil of gloom. The place tastes of old prayers and the memory of rituals long since folded into the stones.

speaker: narrator
text: Lanterns of the Deeps

speaker: narrator
text: Find something that will fit the carved brackets and will bear or produce light when placed there. Once the mounts hold a living glow, the hall may answer — the stones could yield secrets folded into their seams.

speaker: narrator
text: An empty bracket waits for a lantern.

speaker: narrator
text: A prism lantern rests here, ready to be lit.

speaker: narrator
text: Light pours from the prisms, weaving a clear path through the flooded hall. The way to the sanctum stands revealed.

speaker: narrator
text: Light fills the mounts and the chamber sighs. Threads of pearly flame trace the carvings and the stone seems to part its lips. A pale corridor unfurls where shadow once lay; it feels older than living memory and leads toward what might be the sanctum, veiled in salt and promise. The room has answered — more of its secrets lie open now.

speaker: narrator
text: Then every light goes out at once — the sigils, the motes, the glow at your back. The Tide-Born Guardian speaks from the black:

speaker: tide-born guardian
text: The lanterns brought you here. They will not take you further. Walk.

speaker: narrator
text: Sanctum of the Tide

speaker: tide-born guardian
text: Walk east into the water. When you come through, I will ask you one thing.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Water I cannot fight. I will keep the door, then. Better than I kept the last one.

speaker: narrator
text: A voice like Mira, close behind you:

speaker: mira
text: Turn back, Elior. There is nothing out there.

speaker: tide-born guardian
text: You came through. What did you not abandon?

speaker: narrator
text: The waters draw back as if breathing in. Your vow anchors the chamber's heart, and the relic heeds your courage. You may now take the Crystal of Light.

speaker: tide-born guardian
text: Most name a person, and leave themselves behind in the dark. You walked in whole, and you walked out whole. That is the courage the crystal asks for.

speaker: tide-born guardian
text: Name what you will not abandon.

speaker: sir cedric
text: My king.

speaker: sir cedric
text: I did once.

speaker: tide-born guardian
text: One came before you, long ago. Aren. He asked me to test whoever came after him the way he was tested.

speaker: sir cedric
text: It asked me, too. You heard my answer. So did the water, and it said nothing.

speaker: narrator
text: You take the Crystal of Light. The crystal steadies in your grasp, radiance aligning with your resolve.

speaker: narrator
text: You have claimed the Crystal of Light; its steady brilliance answers your courage and steadies what the deep waters once denied. Sir Cedric bids you to press on—dark forces gather, and he needs allies skilled in magic to stand with him when the hour comes.

speaker: mira
text: Well done, Elior. The Crystal answers to courage; you have steadied the tide. Ahead lies the Lower Switchbacks—ridges of ember and knife-rolled stone where ash chokes the air and the path winds like a fever dream. Keep your footing and watch the skies for falling cinders.

speaker: mira
text: And Elior—I can feel the king through the focus. He is weaker than when we set out.

speaker: sir cedric
text: I had the wall that night. I heard nothing. Every day he is weaker, I hear it.

speaker: narrator
text: Lower Switchbacks

speaker: narrator
text: Wind‑carved paths snake across black, glassy rock; ash skims the air and the scent of iron hangs on the wind. A small scholars' camp clings to a lee: canvas shelters patched with soot, low braziers for warmth, and drying racks where scorched notes and map fragments flutter. Workbenches hold polishing stones and brass fittings—evidence of a diligent, makeshift atelier repairing mirror segments found among the outcrops. Beyond the camp, the slope falls into jagged obsidian ribs and steaming vents where fumaroles hiss; sparks drift like trapped fireflies when the wind turns.

speaker: narrator
text: The Ash Scholar straightens and studies you for a long moment before speaking.

speaker: ash scholar
text: We are on an expedition: a small band of scholars and tinkerers, tracing the terraces and cataloguing anything that glints.

speaker: ash scholar
text: I found this brass mirror segment while prying at a collapsed ledge. It is small, but it will mend a mount. There will be more among the outcrops, if you search carefully.

speaker: ash scholar
text: This was in the same ledge. A notebook, burned nearly through. Whoever wrote in it knew these mirrors better than any of us, and I cannot make out who that was. Perhaps you can.

speaker: mira
text: Here, Wisdom is taught in embers. Old guides here tell of a phoenix that nested where the rock blooms with heat — a bird of returning flame. From its ash a single feather rises renewed, and such a feather is said to clear the eyes and steady a wavering hand. Listen for songs on the wind, and tend any sparks you find; they may be more than mere kindle.

speaker: sir cedric
text: We stand about reading vents while he fades. Let me go through that heat first and see what it does.

speaker: malakar
text: Lysa says I measure the light too carefully. Aren says that is why it never misses. We set the third mirror today, and the whole terrace caught fire with it, the good kind.

speaker: malakar
text: The Wasting has reached Willowbrook. Lysa coughs at night and pretends she does not. Aren sits up with her and pretends he is not afraid. They tell me to wait. I have waited all my life.

speaker: narrator
text: The Ash Scholar offers a small nod.

speaker: ash scholar
text: The terraces favour steady hands. Seek the outcrops for what the mountain has shed.

speaker: narrator
text: Obsidian Outcrops

speaker: narrator
text: Needle-sharp obsidian towers rise like black teeth from the ash, their surfaces catching and fracturing the light into jagged, glassy facets. Between the towers, thin seams and crevices hide weathered mirror fragments and the faint scars of old mounts—brass filings, dull polish, and tiny holes that speak of a long-vanished craft. A dry, metallic tang rides the hot wind, and every step sets off a tiny cascade of glass flakes into echoing gullies below.

speaker: narrator
text: Mirrors of Emberlight

speaker: narrator
text: The terraces are lined with ancient, cracked mirrors. Find a way to repair the mirrors and restore the channel of light to the high altar.

speaker: narrator
text: Mirror Terraces

speaker: narrator
text: Stepped platforms rise in concentric benches, each ring studded with sockets for polished mirrors and brass mounts. Channels are neatly etched into the stone to carry and focus light up the slope; stray rays catch on alignment wedges and glint like cold flame. The air humms faintly with residual heat, and dusted ash settles on worktables where scholars and attendants file, polish, and fit mirror segments. A Terrace Warden watches the assembly points, checking the angles and murmuring measurements — the place smells of warm metal, singed cloth, and the mineral tang of cooling slag.

speaker: narrator
text: We are three, and we are one promise.

speaker: father
text: I, Aren, pour courage into the Crystal of Light.

speaker: mother
text: I, Lysa, pour selflessness into the Dragon's Scale.

speaker: malakar
text: I, Malakar, pour wisdom into the Phoenix Feather.

speaker: narrator
text: What we pour into the ward, the ward will keep.

speaker: narrator
text: ✓ Heights of Mount Ember: You discovered your parents' words burned into stone, describing the protective ward they forged through fire and sacrifice.

speaker: narrator
text: With a careful, ringing press you seat the brass segments and secure their alignment. The terrace mount accepts the fittings.

speaker: narrator
text: You apply the binding resin carefully around the seams; the brass segments sit firmer and the joints set.

speaker: narrator
text: A whispered mend gathers in your hands and the mirrors answer — seams knit, polish brightens, and the whole face hums.

speaker: narrator
text: The mirrors are whole. The sun is not where it needs to be. Perhaps rest a while, and let it climb.

speaker: narrator
text: You settle on the warm stone and let the hours pass. The sun climbs until it stands squarely over the terraces. When the sun's beams strike the great mirror they are coaxed and folded together until they pour from the terraces as a single, piercing ray. The light lances into the mountainside, strikes a hidden trigger, and a narrow passage grinds open to the east.

speaker: narrator
text: Elior gathers the scattered brass mirror segments and, with care and skill, restores the ancient light channel atop Mount Ember. The mirrors blaze with reflected sunlight, opening the way to the volcano's heart and the Phoenix's trial of wisdom.

speaker: narrator
text: Ember Gallery

speaker: narrator
text: A vaulted cavern veined with cooling flows; the air smells of charcoal and iron. Streaks of glassed lava lace the walls, catching stray cinders that glow like embers in the gloom. Steam sighs from fissures and pools of blackened water mirror faint, dancing light. Worktables gather scattered fragments of fireglass and ash‑tumbled tools where attendants hammer and sort cooled slag for wards. The heat here is a steady, low thrum — a reminder that the mountain breathes beneath your feet.

speaker: narrator
text: Breath of the Mountain

speaker: narrator
text: The Fumarole Passages exhale waves of heat and steam, blocking the way forward. Find a way to cross the shifting vents and reach the heights to the south.

speaker: narrator
text: Fumarole Passages

speaker: narrator
text: Narrow tunnels exhale a rhythmic, breath-like heat; stone vents chuff and sigh as if the mountain itself sleeps and dreams. Curtains of steam veil the low passages, and the air tastes faintly of sulfur and warm metal. Here and there a vent hisses sparks that glass the rock into smoky, translucent streaks, while the floor bears the pale scars of old fittings—tiny holes and rubbed brass where mounts were once bolted. Each step sends a warm gust that carries a distant clink of metal and the steady, low sigh of fumaroles farther below.

speaker: narrator
text: The vents gust and sputter without rhythm; there is no telling when they will breathe next.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Between breaths, then. I have run through worse than this.

speaker: narrator
text: The Phoenix Guardian studies you for a moment.

speaker: phoenix guardian
text: So, you seek the mighty one? To stand before the Phoenix, you must be both patient and watchful. The mountain tests those who would pass: its breath is wild, its heat unforgiving. First, bring the vents into harmony—let them breathe as one. Only then can you bind the heat with a ward. When the rhythm is steady and the ward is set, the way to the crater will open.

speaker: narrator
text: The Phoenix Guardian watches the vents.

speaker: phoenix guardian
text: The ward holds, but the mountain still breathes. Count its breath. Walk when it draws in.

speaker: narrator
text: You stand still and count.

speaker: narrator
text: The vents fall still, holding their breath. The heat hangs heavy and unmoving.

speaker: narrator
text: The vents draw in. A cool draught tugs past you toward the south.

speaker: narrator
text: With patience and ingenuity, Elior crafts a heat ward from ash-fern and cooled slag, then calibrates the mountain's ancient vents to breathe in a steady, safe rhythm. The searing passages yield, opening the way to the Phoenix's crater and the next trial of wisdom.

speaker: narrator
text: Phoenix Crater

speaker: narrator
text: A luminous bowl of vitrified rock where warm drafts swirl and cinders dance in spirals. The air smells of ozone, resin, and warm iron; the whole bowl feels like a giant hearth that remembers how to forge stars. The warmth is drowsy here, as if the bowl would rather you sat and rested a while.

speaker: narrator
text: You rest for a moment, and as your eyes close, the air grows warmer. When you open them, a vast phoenix of living ember stands before you, its gaze meeting yours with ancient, knowing patience.

speaker: narrator
text: The phoenix's voice does not come from its beak, but resounds within your mind:

speaker: phoenix
text: What is wisdom when time is short?

speaker: narrator
text: The question lingers, bright and weightless, as if the answer might shape the very air around you.

speaker: phoenix
text: I asked this once of the Warden of Wisdom, when he came to me with his two friends. He knew the answer, and did not keep it.

speaker: narrator
text: The phoenix's eyes flare with approval. It plucks a single glowing feather and offers it to you.

speaker: phoenix
text: Wisdom is patience, even when the world burns. Take this, and remember.

speaker: phoenix
text: He gave your answer too. Then time grew short for his friends, and patience was the one thing he had none of. Do not become what he became.

speaker: narrator
text: You think of the third name burned deeper than the others on the terraces.

speaker: narrator
text: You have obtained the Phoenix Feather. Its warmth pulses in your grasp, a living ember that refuses to die. The memory of fire and flight lingers, reminding you that hope can rise from ashes. The path ahead is clearer, but the final virtue remains.

speaker: sir cedric
text: A bird told us to wait, and we waited. I hope it was worth what it cost him.

speaker: narrator
text: The phoenix inclines its head.

speaker: phoenix
text: You saw his name on the terraces, burned deeper than the others. No fire did that. He came back, years after, and struck it again himself, to cut himself out of the promise. The stone would not let him.

speaker: phoenix
text: Remember him when time is short for you.

speaker: narrator
text: The Phoenix Guardian nods:

speaker: phoenix guardian
text: The way is open, but patience is your ally. The Phoenix will not appear for those who rush. Be patient, and the mighty one will reveal itself.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Patience. The king has had nothing from us but patience.

speaker: mira
text: …even when the world burns.

speaker: mira
text: You have done well, Elior. The Phoenix Feather is a token of wisdom; it will guide you through darkness and flame. Ahead lies the Cavern Mouth—gaping stone jaws that breathe cold and shadow. Steel your heart and hold your light high.

speaker: mira
text: There is a word the old folk will reach for when this ash comes down on them: the Wasting. It is not that. The Wasting killed. This drinks.

speaker: mira
text: The king is weaker still. Whatever drains him draws harder with every site we reach.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Weaker still. And I stood on a mountain, waiting on a bird.

speaker: narrator
text: Cavern Mouth

speaker: narrator
text: A broad entry arch yawns before you, curtained by tendrils of cold mist that coil and writhe like spectral fingers. Lantern light wavers and dims at the threshold, as if the darkness within hungers to devour illumination. Ancient symbols are carved into the weathered stone archway, their meanings lost to time but somehow still resonating with a faint, otherworldly power. The air carries whispers of forgotten secrets and the weight of ages past.

speaker: narrator
text: The Mine Overseer grips your arm, voice hoarse:

speaker: mine overseer
text: You don't hear them now, but the rock shifted at dawn. Half a dozen men are trapped behind tons of stone—no air, no light. We tried to dig, but the walls groan with every blow. Some of the younger lads... they screamed until their voices gave out. The rest are silent now. Gods, let them still be alive.

speaker: narrator
text: He points north, jaw clenched:

speaker: mine overseer
text: Collapsed Galleries are blocked, but the Tool Cache has what you need—braces, straps, blocks. If you can reach them, you might hold the roof long enough to pull the miners free.

speaker: narrator
text: He presses a heavy iron key into your palm, his hand trembling:

speaker: mine overseer
text: Here—take my key. It opens the supply crate. Get those miners out.

speaker: mira
text: The shadows here run deep, Elior. The miners' plight is a test of selflessness—lend your strength, and the path to the dragon will open. The caverns will not yield their heart until all are safe.

speaker: sir cedric
text: People under the rock. That I understand. Point me at the heavy end.

speaker: narrator
text: Miners' Rescue

speaker: narrator
text: Collapsed Galleries have trapped people behind tons of stone. You must find a way to free them.

speaker: narrator
text: The Mine Overseer nods grimly.

speaker: mine overseer
text: The miners are still waiting. The Tool Cache is north.

speaker: narrator
text: Tool Cache

speaker: narrator
text: A reinforced alcove carved from living stone, where shadows pool between weathered crates of timbers, iron braces, and coils of hemp rope. The air tastes of old metal and earth, heavy with the weight of countless mining expeditions. Ancient tool marks score the walls, and you sense the presence of those who labored here in ages past. The flickering torchlight reveals corners shrouded in darkness.

speaker: narrator
text: You search deeper into the shadowed alcove and discover a heavy supply crate hidden behind stacked timbers, locked with a large iron padlock that glints with an almost malevolent gleam. The label reads: 'Rescue Supplies — For Emergency Use Only.' The padlock is iron, rusted shut, and it has a keyhole.

speaker: narrator
text: Collapsed Galleries

speaker: narrator
text: Ancient passages lie strangled by fallen stone, their throats choked with the weight of ages. Dust motes drift like restless spirits in the stagnant air, and shadows pool in the broken archways where starlight once danced. The walls bear scars of some long-forgotten catastrophe, and you sense the presence of those who await deliverance from this tomb of earth and shadow. A palpable tension hangs in the darkness, as if the very stones remember their violent collapse.

speaker: narrator
text: You examine the massive pile of fallen rock. The collapse appears unstable, with loose stones precariously balanced above. You can hear desperate voices calling from beyond the barrier—miners are definitely trapped on the other side. The ceiling sags dangerously, but with the right reinforcement, you might be able to stabilize the collapse and then clear a safe passage through.

speaker: narrator
text: The miners gather around as the lead miner steps forward, dust-covered but relieved:

speaker: miners
text: Thank the gods you found us. When that section collapsed this morning, we thought we were done for. The whole ceiling came down like thunder—trapped us behind tons of rock with barely any air.

speaker: narrator
text: Another miner adds, voice shaking:

speaker: miners
text: We could hear you working on the other side, but we didn't dare hope. Those braces you placed saved our lives—without them, the whole tunnel would've come down on our heads.

speaker: narrator
text: The lead miner lowers his voice and nods toward a boy sitting apart from the rest:

speaker: miners
text: That's Tobin. Youngest of us. He was the one shouting for help, hours of it, till his voice went. Hasn't said a word since. Not one.

speaker: narrator
text: The lead miner nods gratefully:

speaker: miners
text: We can't thank you enough, Elior. Now that the immediate danger's passed, we'll get to work reinforcing this whole section. These old caverns need proper support beams before anyone else ventures through. The route to the Echo Chambers is open, but we'll make sure it stays that way.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Someone should stay until the braces settle. I will.

speaker: oldest miner
text: You have a king to fetch, ser. We have stood in worse holes than this one.

speaker: narrator
text: You stabilized the collapse and led the miners to safety. The route to the inner caverns is now open.

speaker: sir cedric
text: They are out. The old man was right. I have a king to fetch.

speaker: narrator
text: The miners look up from their work, tools in hand:

speaker: miners
text: Still here, Elior? We're making good progress on these support beams. The passage to the Echo Chambers is secure now—you can head east whenever you're ready. We'll keep working to make sure these old caverns are safe for future travelers.

speaker: narrator
text: Echo Chambers

speaker: narrator
text: Smooth caverns carved from living stone stretch into shadow, where every footfall reverberates through the darkness like whispered incantations. Faint, otherworldly voices seem to mimic your speech, echoing from unseen alcoves as if ancient spirits dwell within the walls themselves. Mysterious runic walls line the chamber, their symbols glowing with a dim, ethereal light that pulses in rhythm with your heartbeat. The air thrums with an almost palpable energy, and you sense that this place has witnessed rituals of great power.

speaker: narrator
text: Your careful search of the shadowed alcoves reveals a bundle of ancient scrolls tucked away in a stone niche, their parchment yellowed with age and covered in faded script. These appear to be old oath scrolls, containing wisdom about sacred promises and the true nature of selfless vows.

speaker: a man's voice, steady
text: Mal. Put the lamp down and listen to me.

speaker: a second man, quick and low
text: I have listened for a year, Aren. The Wasting is in Willowbrook. It is in her.

speaker: a woman's voice, hoarse
text: Then let it stay in me. Not this. Time is not a door, Mal.

speaker: the second man
text: It is only a door if I close it again.

speaker: the steady voice
text: It is a wound. You know it is. Stay. Wait with us.

speaker: the second man
text: You would have me wait while you die.

speaker: narrator
text: Tobin turns the pale stone over in his fingers. As his hand closes around it, the endless dripping of the gallery seems to step back a pace, and his shoulders come down for the first time since you met him.

speaker: tobin
text: It's quiet.

speaker: narrator
text: His voice is a cracked whisper.

speaker: tobin
text: I could still hear it. Me, shouting. All this time, I could still hear it.

speaker: narrator
text: Across the gallery, the lead miner sets down his pick and does not pick it up again.

speaker: narrator
text: Tobin touches the charm at his throat:

speaker: tobin
text: Still quiet. I'll keep it, if that's all right. Just till we're up top.

speaker: narrator
text: Stillness Vestibule

speaker: narrator
text: A hush falls over this chamber like a shroud. Dark pools mirror the ceiling, so still they look frozen in time, and the stone seems to swallow every sound. At the centre, three weathered echo stones stand in a triangle. Their carved channels look made to catch whispered words and hold them.

speaker: narrator
text: The Silence Keeper whispers, their voice barely disturbing the air:

speaker: silence keeper
text: I have kept this hush for forty years, so the sleeper below can rest. I was a singer once, in the villages above. I sang one night too loud, too near the deep, and something old turned over in its sleep. I put my voice down that night and never picked it up.

speaker: silence keeper
text: The stones in this room were cut to carry a whisper to the sleeper without waking it. They have gone cold. But a chant will not carry over troubled water, and these pools are not as still as they seem. Bless them, and give them the old chant, and the way will open.

speaker: narrator
text: The phantoms turn toward you, their voices rising in a chorus of whispered syllables that seem to flow like water over stone. The words are just beyond comprehension, as if spoken in a language forgotten by time.

speaker: narrator
text: Beneath the whispers, a few of them are humming: a slow tune that climbs three notes and settles home again.

speaker: narrator
text: Through the murmur, one word comes clear, over and over: rest … rest …

speaker: narrator
text: You sense that these hallowed stones now await the ancient chant that will complete the ritual and banish the restless spirits from this sacred place.

speaker: narrator
text: Oath of Stillness

speaker: narrator
text: The Echo Chambers whisper with restless phantoms that block the path to the dragon's hall. Ancient voices drift through the darkness, their words lost to time but their purpose clear—they seek the sacred ritual that will grant them peace. The runic walls hold secrets of old ceremonies, and somewhere within these carved passages lies the key to silencing their eternal unrest. The echo stones await a blessed chant, one that must be spoken with reverence and precision to quiet the wandering spirits.

speaker: narrator
text: The pools are mirror-still. Now the chant will carry.

speaker: silence keeper
text: The stones in this room were cut to carry a whisper to the sleeper without waking it. They have gone cold. The water lies true now; it will hold your words. Bless them, and give them the old chant, and the way will open.

speaker: narrator
text: The words echo and re-echo, building into a harmonious silence that banishes the wandering phantoms. The path to the dragon's hall now lies open.

speaker: narrator
text: The Resonant Chant has quieted the wandering phantoms, its sacred words echoing through the stillness like ripples across a mirror-dark pond. One by one, the restless spirits begin to shimmer and fade, their ethereal forms growing translucent as centuries of anguish finally release their hold. Ancient faces turn toward you with expressions of profound gratitude before dissolving into motes of silver light that drift upward like falling stars in reverse. The phantoms' whispered syllables transform into gentle sighs of relief as they slip between the boundaries of reality, crossing from this dimension into the peaceful void beyond. Their luminous essence swirls in spiraling patterns before vanishing entirely, leaving behind only the faintest trace of ozone and the profound silence they had so desperately sought. The illusions have fallen silent, the ancient burden lifted, and the path to the dragon's hall now lies open, bathed in the sacred luminescence of your completed ritual.

speaker: narrator
text: The Silence Keeper bows their hooded head:

speaker: silence keeper
text: The sleeper spoke with you, and the stone held. Forty years, and I have never been so glad to have kept a quiet. The water lies true now; it will hold your words.

speaker: narrator
text: Dragon's Hall

speaker: narrator
text: A hall of living stone opens beyond sight, its ceiling lost in shadow. Embers burn slowly along the floor, pulsing like a heartbeat, and somewhere in the dark, water drips. Rings of old sigils spiral across the black tiles around the Ancient Dragon. It lies coiled at the centre, scales like polished obsidian, and each slow breath hums in your bones.

speaker: narrator
text: The ancient dragon's voice resonates through your mind like distant thunder:

speaker: ancient dragon
text: Young one, I remember your parents well. Aren and Lysa, Wardens of the Dawn. They came to me with their friend Malakar, the three of them laughing, and made the relics as equals.

speaker: ancient dragon
text: When Malakar tore a wound in time, it was they who stood against him. They poured themselves into a ward. It hides you from his sight, and it holds his wound shut. It is anchored in the amulet you carry, and in the bindings of your king, who was their friend and gave his crown's oath to hold it. That is why Malakar drains him.

speaker: ancient dragon
text: They are not gone as the dead are gone, child. They are warded away, not dead.

speaker: ancient dragon
text: They had a saying, the three of them, carved wherever they worked: Power follows purpose; purpose follows truth. When he offers you what you want most, say it to him. It was his before it was yours.

speaker: narrator
text: Then, beneath the dragon's breathing, another voice: the whisper from your dream, at the very edge of hearing. “Elior… little one. Help me. I cannot hold it shut alone.” And after it, almost lost in the dragon's breathing: “…be patient where I was not…” You know it the way you know a song someone sang to you before you had words for it. Then it is gone.

speaker: narrator
text: You look up at the ancient dragon. Its golden eyes are half closed.

speaker: ancient dragon
text: The friend who stayed behind.

speaker: ancient dragon
text: And the healer who waits at the cavern mouth. Little Mira. Tell her she has grown old.

speaker: narrator
text: The ancient dragon rumbles softly:

speaker: ancient dragon
text: You have read the old words. Then tell me: what will you give back, for what you take?

speaker: narrator
text: ✓ Shadows of the Caverns: The ancient dragon shared memories of your parents' final act, naming them and the completion of their ward.

speaker: narrator
text: The three testimonies have revealed the truth: Elior's parents, once apprentices to Malakar, defied their master to protect their son. Through sacrifice and ancient wards, they hid Elior from Malakar's sight, ensuring he would grow strong enough to face the darkness when the time came.

speaker: ancient dragon
text: Your words ring true, young one. The scale is yours to bear. May you carry its burden with honor.

speaker: ancient dragon
text: The oath has been given and accepted. The scale is yours to claim.

speaker: narrator
text: You take the Dragon's Scale. The dragon's scale settles into your hands with surprising weight. You feel the burden of responsibility and the strength that comes from selfless action. The relic pulses warmly against your palm.

speaker: narrator
text: You have claimed the Dragon's Scale, its obsidian surface gleaming with ancient power. The dragon's wisdom echoes in your mind, a testament to the selflessness you have proven. With all three relics in hand, the final trial awaits—the Warding Rite that will determine the fate of all.

speaker: ancient dragon
text: Go with my blessing. The prison I hold is weaker for the scale's going. That is the price, and it is mine to pay, not yours.

speaker: mira
text: The three relics are yours, Elior. The dragon's wisdom runs deep—its scale will turn aside shadow and bind your oath. Let us return to my hut where we can combine their power into something that can save the king.

speaker: mira
text: The king is fading, Elior. We have less time than I hoped.

speaker: sir cedric
text: He was taken on my watch. He will not die on it.

speaker: mira
text: Before I join them, Elior, there is something you must hear from me, and not from a stone or a dragon.

speaker: mira
text: You noticed. I saw you notice.

speaker: mira
text: I knew your parents. Not as a healer knows a neighbour. I was their pupil — Aren's, Lysa's, and Malakar's. The three of them taught me everything I know of circles and wards.

speaker: mira
text: When Aren and Lysa poured themselves into the ward, someone had to stay with the child it hid. I came to Willowbrook as its healer, and I have watched over you every day since.

speaker: mira
text: Your grandmother knew. She is Lysa's mother, and she kept the secret with me.

speaker: elior
text: Why didn't you tell me?

speaker: mira
text: Because the seal could not bear it. Malakar's cloaked agent walked Willowbrook's lanes searching for the amulet, and any word of who you were could have reached him.

speaker: mira
text: Lyria wrote to me from Greendale, about a girl with a mask on her wrist. I burned the letter. If I had gone, I would have shown Greendale what the healer at Willowbrook can do, with his agent in both towns and you in one of them. I have never been so ashamed of anything.

speaker: mira
text: I am telling you now because you have earned the truth. The amulet you carry is the anchor of the ward your parents became.

speaker: mira
text: Say what you need to say to me, Elior. I would rather hear it now.

speaker: narrator
text: (Answer her with: say i forgive you or say you should have told me to Mira.)

speaker: mira
text: When you are ready, tell me, and I will begin the Warding Rite.

speaker: mira
text: And ask me anything you like now — about your parents, Malakar, the amulet, your grandmother. I will not hide from you again.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Do what she needs, Elior. I have waited this long. I can wait one more hour.

speaker: mira
text: The three relics resonate with ancient power, Elior. The Crystal of Light, the Phoenix Feather, and the Dragon's Scale—courage, wisdom, and selflessness made manifest.

speaker: mira
text: By light and flame and ancient oath, let these virtues merge into one vessel of protection!

speaker: mira
text: It is done. This elixir can counter Malakar's life-draining ritual and save King Alden. Take it, and we shall proceed to the fortress.

speaker: narrator
text: Main quest complete

speaker: narrator
text: You have completed the quest 'The Three Virtues'.

speaker: mira
text: Elior, you must take the Lifelight Elixir before we depart for the fortress. We cannot face Malakar without it—the elixir is our only hope of countering his life-draining ritual and saving King Alden.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Then it is the fortress. I have been walking toward that door since the night he was taken.

speaker: mira
text: The Lifelight Elixir pulses with the power of three virtues. Now we make our final journey—to Malakar's fortress, where the kingdom's fate awaits.

speaker: mira
text: I know the road. I walked it as a girl, when it was the Wardens' hall and not his fortress. Your parents made the relics there, at a workbench under the dome.

speaker: mira
text: Steel yourself, Elior. Beyond this circle lies the heart of shadow itself. But you carry the light that can pierce even Malakar's darkness.

speaker: sir cedric
text: If I had held the door that night, we would not be standing at this one.

speaker: narrator
text: Entrance to Malakar's Fortress

speaker: narrator
text: A blackstone bastion rises from a shattered ridge; gate sigils pulse like a heartbeat behind iron lattices. The air tastes of cold metal and distant thunder. The massive gates loom ahead, wreathed in shadow and bound with eldritch wards. Where the gate arch meets the wall an older carving shows through the black: a sun rising over three linked rings.

speaker: narrator
text: You examine the massive gates that tower above you. Their blackened iron is carved with sigils that seem to writhe in the corner of your vision. Beyond the lattice, you glimpse corridors that pulse with malevolent energy. This is the threshold of Malakar's domain—where King Alden is held captive and the kingdom's fate will be decided.

speaker: narrator
text: The Ancient Amulet is warm against your palm. You came on this journey believing Malakar took your parents from you. You know better now. Aren and Lysa were his closest friends, and the ward they became is still holding.

speaker: narrator
text: The Dragon said they were warded away, not dead. You do not yet know what that means.

speaker: narrator
text: The Lifelight Elixir pulses with protective power, ready to shield you from the sorcerer's influence. Act III is complete. The final confrontation awaits.

speaker: mira
text: I know how I look, Elior. Do not ask me to stay behind.

speaker: mira
text: Your parents walked into the dark without me once. I will not let you do the same. Go with courage, wisdom, and selflessness—I am coming with you.

speaker: narrator
text: A low murmur ripples through the ghostly figures as they notice your presence. Their whispers grow more urgent, overlapping in harmonies that speak of longing and unfinished purpose, but no clear meaning emerges.

speaker: narrator
text: The phantoms drift closer, their ethereal forms shimmering as they attempt to communicate. Their voices blend into a haunting melody of sibilant sounds and half-formed words that dance at the edge of understanding.

speaker: narrator
text: Spectral lips move in silent prayer, then burst into urgent whispers that cascade around you like falling leaves. Each voice carries a different tone of desperation, yet none speak words you can fully grasp.
